NavigationService.phobosnav_help_status_:
phobosnav: status | settings | fly [km] | dock | stop | resume | cruise <m/s> | arrivalspeed <m/s> | arrival <km> | defaults | torch on/off | forget | spawn. Defaults explicitly resets this console’s preferences; forget clears its saved flight. N2: rendezvous [km] | follow [km] | spawnpursuit. N3: firetarget | weapons <1–9> | volley | fireweapon | aimweapon | autoaim | engage | ceasefire | nativefire. Engage requires N3 and a separately selected qualified target, including during manual flight. Cease retains offensive Hold; nativefire releases it and may resume native autofire. Rendezvous/Follow match motion. Native N3 spawn: spawn PhobosNavModFireControl.
phobosnav approachdock — approach the cleared target and hand over to terminal RCS docking.
Audio: phobosnav watch | unwatch | cue-volume. Engage Approach/Rendezvous before watching.

Hub.placement_notice: Polaris Flight Hub: open the navigation console's layout Edit menu and place one tall hub (one column, four rows). Move or hide the old left-column instruments first; keep the native map, sensors, warnings and specialist panels accessible. Existing compact positions are not enlarged. N1 and N2 share one hub.
Hub.help:
Navigation: Approach stops at the selected separation; Dock starts checked terminal RCS guidance. Approach & Dock binds the target and assigned ports, approaches 1 km beyond the protective hull-clearance radius, matches motion and rechecks before terminal handoff. Inside staging it uses terminal admission directly. Keep the native docking interface available for attachment; the hub never bypasses clearance, fees, consequences or port fit.

Closing speed is positive toward the target and negative when separating. Relative speed includes sideways drift. A dash means unavailable, including pending power or contact updates. Alignment is the existing terminal controller's ship-to-target heading error, not a measurement of port geometry.

Pursuit requires N2; the Fire page requires N3. N3 works independently during manual flight or coasting. Select the offensive target separately, choose its native weapon group and volley limit, then lift the cover and Engage. Auto Aim is separate. Cease Fire stops aiming and retains offensive hold while Follow continues. Return to Native explicitly releases that hold and may resume native autofire. Native power, arcs, aim, ammunition, reload, missile lock and weapon-mode restrictions still apply. Braking takes priority. If native guarded artwork is unavailable, Engage stays inhibited.

Systems controls take manual authority and clear automation before changing reactor flow/thrust. Native reactor readiness, limiter and no-wake restrictions still apply; this hub cannot start a cold reactor. Connected power is the native console's connected stored energy, not whole-ship generation. Use the native reactor and specialist instruments for startup, faults and detailed engineering.

Disengage clears commanded thrust and allows coasting; it is not an emergency brake. Combined docking and pursuit always suspend on loading. Resume rechecks the same module, target and ports. Page changes and display refresh never authorize commands.

If native flight intent blocks engagement, Disengage explicitly releases standard native autopilot, station-keeping and held thrust, clears saved switches on this ship's consoles and sets torch cycle to zero. Reactor power stays on; velocity and spin remain. Unknown AI and independent flight plugins must release themselves. Resume needs a suspended flight; Cease Fire needs active flight or fire control. N1 alone does not enable N2 pursuit or N3 weapons.

FCS.pursuit_help:
Rendezvous and Follow require N2.

Rendezvous matches motion and finishes. Follow maintains separation.

Weapons and optional aiming require N3 on the Fire page.
FCS.help:
N3 Fire Control System: select a qualified offensive target and one native weapon group. Volleys (1–9) counts successful native batches, not projectiles or ammunition units; each batch contains the weapons ready at that instant. Engage requires the guarded switch. Weapons can operate during manual flight with Auto Aim off.

Auto Aim is a separate permission for RCS rotation while coasting, or a heading request during N2 Follow. Choose a weapon with Weapon > and Use for aim. Pilot thrust/yaw cancels aiming and firing. Braking and clearance take priority.

Cease Fire and volley completion retain offensive hold and stop Auto Aim; Follow continues. Return to Native explicitly releases the group and may allow native autofire. Defensive PDCs and deliberate manual fire remain native. Release the old group before changing groups.

Reload retains offensive hold only: targets, firing permission, remaining volleys and live aiming are never restored. Missing/stale readings are unavailable. Missiles require native automatic eligibility and a full native lock; decoys are excluded. No promised hit probability, intact boarding or crew survival. Native map, sensors and specialist weapon settings remain separate.
